proposal.name: Hold configured repositories' trusted changes for a person

plan.name: Hold configured repositories' trusted changes for a person
plan.summary: Complete step 9 of parent #564 as one plumbing change: derive configured repositories' trusted paths from the captured base contract, always protecting CI and the gate workflow (including .github/, .gitlab-ci.yml and .circleci/), the repository contract, root and nested AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, root and nested .codex/, .claude/ and .mcp.json, and the contract's agent rules, dependency inputs, lockfiles and additional trusted paths. Admit explicitly planned CI files only through the configured native profile, carry derived trust into proposals and saved plans without making displayed Trusted metadata authoritative, and update the planner and builder instructions while preserving Invariant's existing TrustedBase, CI refusal, legacy hashes, locks and disabled external issue intake. Compute scope and human-merge eligibility from all actual changed paths, including deletions and allowed new regression tests, using the original base policy and revalidating the execution contract against the current base; reject incompatible base changes, preserve compatible movement and original regression novelty, prevent candidate removal or weakening of trust declarations and forged metadata from authorizing a merge, open successful configured trusted builds as drafts, and keep recovered, watched and rebuilt trusted drafts for a person through publication, retries and a fresh fetch and validation immediately before readiness or merge, reusing the existing protocol hold without modifying proved transitions. Recognize workflow-push permission refusals as durable actionable human handoffs that preserve the work, explain the required publishing credentials and retry, never report ready or merged success and never retry the refused write without a writer's command; ordinary in-scope work remains eligible for automatic merge and needs no workflow permission, and Invariant's App permissions remain unchanged. Extend the named existing contract, plan, scope and intake tests without weakening their Invariant compatibility assertions, and update SPEC.md with existing decision citations, the README within 400 lines, docs/factory.md and docs/factory-app.md to describe this configured boundary and workflow-edit prerequisite; this step needs its own decision, which the merger records before the next step because the plumbing build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestRepositoryImplicitTrust695
tests.says: Captured repository trust always includes CI, root and nested agent instructions and tool configuration, declared rules, dependencies and custom paths, without importing Invariant's code layout or trusting ordinary files; later base edits cannot mutate a captured snapshot.

tests.name: TestConfiguredProposalTrustAndCI695
tests.says: Configured native drafts admit named CI changes, show the derived human-merge paths and preserve them through lock serialization; Trusted remains outside the hash and Invariant's legacy plan validation still refuses CI.

tests.name: TestConfiguredScopeTrustCannotBeForged695
tests.says: Scope classifies the actual diff from authoritative base rules, including nested instructions, custom paths, planned CI, deletions and implicit regressions; removing a trust declaration or forging Trusted cannot weaken that result, unplanned CI remains out of scope and untouched planned paths do not create a hold.

tests.name: TestConfiguredScopeRevalidatesCurrentBase695
tests.says: An unrelated compatible base advance keeps ordinary work eligible, while added or removed trust, changed check authority or a removed repository contract stops a candidate ratified against the old contract.

tests.name: TestConfiguredPublicationKeepsTrustedDrafts695
tests.says: Successful configured trusted builds publish as human-held drafts and recovered drafts stay drafts, with actual trusted paths in the handoff, while ordinary successful builds can be ready.

tests.name: TestConfiguredRetryRecomputesTrust695
tests.says: A writer's retry and passing CI cannot ready or merge configured trusted drafts despite empty Trusted metadata, while an ordinary in-scope draft can be readied and merged despite forged Trusted metadata.

tests.name: TestConfiguredLastMergeCheckRefreshesBase695
tests.says: A base policy change after the first successful scope check is fetched and detected before marking a draft ready or merging either a draft or ready pull request.

tests.name: TestConfiguredRebuildRetainsHumanHold695
tests.says: A failed configured trusted draft is replaced exactly once on retry, and its passing replacement still opens as a draft for a person with the actual trusted paths.

tests.name: TestWorkflowPermissionRefusalHandsOff695
tests.says: GitHub's workflow permission refusal during publication produces an actionable durable handoff naming publishing credentials and retry, leaves no ready or merged success and stops repeated pushes until a person directs a retry.

usage.summary: Wrote [plan.json](plan.json) and nine acceptance tests covering the complete trusted-change hold in one PR. Check 1 passed: all nine tests fail on the unchanged base, as required.
